thread:
John (ACME): Hey team — hitting an intermittent issue with SSE streaming from /v1/streams. Stream starts, we get a few token events, then after ~20-40s the connection drops and the client never receives the final [DONE]. curl shows HTTP/1.1 200 OK then connection reset. Request-id: req-ace7b. I've attached a pcap and the client logs. Any idea why streams are truncating? We're seeing weird token accounting on our end too.

Maya (Support): thanks for the report! :wave: escalated to SRE + runtime. Can you paste the minimal curl you used and confirm if you see any 5xx in server logs? Also confirm whether the client is reconnecting automatically or trying to resume.

John (ACME): repro curl I used:

  curl -v --no-buffer \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n    -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n    -H "Connection: keep-alive" \n    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=rw-13b"

Client is reconnecting on 5s backoff but we never see the final tokens. Sometimes we get an extra chunk then immediate close. Logs attached: client shows ECONNRESET on read.

Devon (SRE): thanks — looping in Eli. First quick checks: can you share the full request id (req-ace7b ok) and exact client IP/time window? I'll pull LB/ingress metrics.

Ingrid (Observability-Bot): Trace created: https://otel.example/trace/0f3a1b (span summary pasted)
- root span: ingress.handler (duration 31.2s)
- downstream: runtime.stream_writer (30.9s)
- error annotated: stream closed by transport after write failed (EPIPE)
Metrics snapshot (last 5m):
- counters.stream_close_total{reason=\"client_reset\"} = 28
- gauges.active_streams = 12
- histo.stream_write_latency_p50 = 120ms, p95 = 420ms

Eli (Eng Runtime): from runtime logs for req-ace7b: 

  [2026-03-12T15:19:43.842Z] req=ace7b runtime: starting stream write
  [2026-03-12T15:20:14.275Z] req=ace7b runtime: write chunk size=1024
  [2026-03-12T15:20:14.276Z] req=ace7b runtime: write error: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->52.12.34.56:51832: write: broken pipe
  [2026-03-12T15:20:14.276Z] req=ace7b runtime: closing stream (client_reset)

Looks like the TCP connection is being torn down mid-stream. Could be client, intermediate proxy, or ALB idle/timeout. Also noting a correlated flurry of keepalive RSTs from same client IP.

Maya (Support): John — can you confirm if you're behind a corporate proxy or NAT that might have shorter idle timeouts? Also does your client set TCP keepalive or SSE comment heartbeats?

John (ACME): We're behind our corp proxy. Not sure how it treats long-lived connections. We don't send comment heartbeats right now.

Devon (SRE): OK probable culprits: 1) corporate proxy cutting idle TCP after ~30s 2) ALB/nginx idle timeout lower than stream length 3) client-side socket limits. Quick repro steps for you (John) to rule out network: run the following from a machine not behind the proxy (or via SSH tunnel to cloud):

  # reproduce raw SSE from public network
  curl -v --no-buffer \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n    -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=rw-13b&prompt=test-short"

If that keeps open and completes, it's likely your proxy. If it still cuts, we'll capture pcap on our edge and ask you for client pcap.

Maya (Support): Also attaching a tiny node repro that toggles a heartbeat comment (try it outside corp):

  const fetch = require('node-fetch');
  (async ()=>{
    const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=rw-13b', {
      headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <REDACTED>', 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' }
    });
    res.body.on('data', (chunk)=>{
      process.stdout.write(chunk.toString());
    });
    // send heartbeat via nextjs proxy or client isn't always needed, server can send comment lines too
  })();

Eli (Eng Runtime): on our side I've requested a tcpdump from the edge host for the 15:18:30-15:21:00 window and got a pcap. Observations: FIN from client IP at 15:20:14 immediate after a 0-byte window probe; no TCP RST from server. That aligns with client/proxy closing. Sample tcpdump excerpt:

  15:20:14.276000 IP 52.12.34.56.51832 > 10.0.0.5.443: Flags [F.], seq 12345, ack 67890, win 0

So server didn't actively RST — client side closed.

Devon (SRE): thanks, that matches. Two action items:
1) Support: advise customer to enable SSE heartbeat/comments or client TCP keepalive to prevent idle close.
2) Engineering: consider server-side periodic comment ("\n: keepalive\n\n") every 15s when generating long responses to keep intermediates from idling.

Eli (Eng Runtime): Agreed. We already have a flag to emit comment heartbeats for long-running streams but it's not enabled by default for small responses. I'll ship a small change to enable periodic heartbeats for streams longer than 10s. Patch reference: git/infra/stream-heartbeat rev abc123 -> rolling out to canary.

Billing Bot: Note on billing — partial streams: tokens already emitted are billable. For req-ace7b, token usage recorded = 674 tokens. I've opened a manual review ticket to check whether truncation was caused by infra and whether a goodwill credit should be applied if this was due to our edge/proxy configuration. Ticket: BILL-1024.

John (ACME): thanks all. I'll run the out-of-proxy repro and attach the client pcap. If heartbeat change lands, please ping me so we can retest. :pray:

Maya (Support): will do. Quick mitigation for you in the meantime: try adding a small client-side keepalive or send SSE comment every 10s. We'll follow up after runtime patch and after you attach pcap.

Devon (SRE): follow-ups for us: check ALB idle timeout settings across regions (possible 30s default), verify nginx proxy keepalive settings, and add an alert for "stream_close_total reason=client_reset spike" > 10/min.

Eli (Eng Runtime): created PR to enable server heartbeats for long streams, tests added. Rolling to canary now, will bump to stable after 24h canary monitoring.

Ingrid (Observability-Bot): Canary metrics will be posted to #eng-runtime/canary when available. Added temporary dashboard panel: stream_close_rate / active_streams / p95_write_latency.

John (ACME): attached client pcap + client logs in thread. Reproducer from non-corp machine completed successfully (no truncation). Looks like proxy indeed. Thanks everyone.

Maya (Support): marking as actionable (SRE + runtime). Leaving open until patch + customer verify. :white_check_mark:
